title: Fang-2024-involvement-10.7554/elife.89076
description: Stereo-EEG recordings from six adult male patients with drug-resistant epilepsy performing a visual awareness task with saccadic report. Near-threshold Gabor gratings were presented and awareness was reported by saccade direction. The dataset includes per-trial behaviour, defaced T1 MRI, and, in sourcedata, post-implantation CT plus eye-position and behaviour files from the patients and 10 healthy controls. It supports investigation of the role of the prefrontal cortex in the emergence of visual awareness.
methods_description: Depth electrodes (8-20 contacts) were recorded with a NEURACLE amplifier at 1 kHz with a 1-250 Hz hardware filter and 50 Hz notch, referenced to a white-matter contact. Patients viewed a 50 ms Gabor grating at 7° eccentricity, with contrast set by a 1-up/1-down staircase around the perceptual threshold. After 600 ms, a colour cue indicated the saccade-target mapping for reporting seen versus not seen. Eye position was recorded with an infrared eye tracker at 1 kHz. Original BDF recordings were converted to BrainVision format.
